result:
Admins can now change a user's role from a select in each row of the users table. I haven't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked, so none of this has been executed or type-checked.

- **API:** `features/users/api/update-user-role.ts` adds `updateUserRole`, which sends `PATCH /users/{userId}/role` with `{ role }`. The role is validated with a Zod schema (`ADMIN` or `USER`). The `useUpdateUserRole` hook refetches the users list on success, so the table shows the new role.
- **Success message:** the "User Role Updated" notification is shown inside the hook's `onSuccess`. `docs/api-layer.md` says feature components must not call `useNotifications`, so this differs from `delete-user.tsx`, which does.
- **UI:** `features/users/components/update-user-role.tsx` is a new select, built from the `ROLES` enum. It is disabled while the request is in flight. `users-list.tsx` now renders it in the Role column.
- **Mock API:** I added a `PATCH /users/:userId/role` handler to `testing/mocks/handlers/users.ts`. It requires an admin, limits the change to the caller's team, and persists the update. Without it the feature wouldn't work against the mock backend.

I used a plain `<select>` instead of the shared `Select` component, because that one only works with react-hook-form registration and has a label wrapper. An admin can also change their own role from the table. I didn't restrict that, but `DeleteUser` does hide itself for the current user, so say if you want the same here.
